introduction: Plants do not have a nervous system or a brain. So, how do they bend toward sunlight, or know when to drop their leaves or ripen their fruit? They do this entirely through chemical messengers called Plant Hormones (Phytohormones).

core_concepts.title: Auxin (The Growth Hormone)
core_concepts.description:
Function: Responsible for 'Cell Elongation' and 'Apical Dominance' (making the plant grow taller at the tip rather than wider). 
Tropism: Auxin is responsible for Phototropism. It accumulates on the shaded side of the stem, causing that side to grow faster, making the plant 'bend towards the light'.

core_concepts.title: Gibberellins
core_concepts.description: Function: Responsible for the massive 'Elongation of the Stem/Internodes' (it can make genetically dwarf plants grow tall) and helps in breaking seed dormancy (triggering seed germination).

core_concepts.title: Cytokinins
core_concepts.description:
Function: Promotes rapid 'Cell Division' (Cytokinesis). 
Key Fact: It is known as the anti-aging hormone of plants because it delays the senescence (aging, wilting, and yellowing) of leaves.

core_concepts.title: Ethylene (The Ripening Hormone)
core_concepts.description: Function: It is the **ONLY Gaseous Hormone** found in plants. Its primary function is the 'Natural Ripening of Fruits'.

core_concepts.title: Abscisic Acid (ABA - The Stress Hormone)
core_concepts.description: Function: It is a 'Growth Inhibitor'. It prepares the plant to survive extreme environmental stress (like severe drought) by closing the stomata to prevent water loss, and it promotes the 'abscission' (falling off) of older leaves and ripe fruits.

important_entities.name: Plant Movements (Tropism)
important_entities.significance:
1. Phototropism: Movement towards light (Shoot is positive, Root is negative). 
2. Geotropism: Movement towards gravity (Root is positive, Shoot is negative). 
3. Hydrotropism: Movement towards water (Roots are highly positively hydrotropic).

trap_alerts_and_exceptions.explanation: Exam Trap: If an exam asks 'Which hormone *naturally* ripens fruits?', the answer is **Ethylene**. However, if asked 'Which chemical is used for the *ARTIFICIAL* ripening of fruits?', the answer is **Calcium Carbide** (which reacts with moisture to produce Acetylene gas).

mnemonics_and_tricks.explanation: The name itself tells you its function: Cytokinin triggers cytokinesis (the actual physical division of cells).

exam_strategy_tips: A highly repeated question in almost all competitive exams (NDA, SSC, PCS): 'Which is the only plant hormone that naturally exists in a gaseous state?' Answer: Ethylene.
